newsitem.title: USA: Harry Helmsley wills everything to his wife.
newsitem.headline: Harry Helmsley wills everything to his wife.

text.p: Billionaire real estate mogul Harry Helmsley, whose holdings include the Empire State Building and some of New York City's most posh hotels, left all his assets to his widow Leona, according to his will filed for probate.
Helmsley died Saturday in Scottsdale, Arizona, of pneumonia at age 87.

Helmsley also appointed his wife executor of the will, which stated that Helmsley left all his real estate holdings and personal property including antiques, works of art and other collectibles to Mrs. Helmsley, with the understanding that she could do with it as she sees fit.
The only other beneficiary named in the will was Helmsley's long-time secretary, Ceil Fried of Manhattan, who was left $25,000.

Helmsley's holdings include a partnership in the Empire State Building, which he bought in 1961 for $65 million. His other New York holdings include the Lincoln Building, which has a market value of $140 million. His 1 Penn Plaza building, at Madison Square Garden, has a market value of $480 million.

At the time of his death, Helmsley also controlled 27 hotels and 50,000 apartments and had other real estate holdings in Detroit, Chicago, San Francisco, Houston, Los Angeles, Washington, DC, and other cities.
Forbes magazine ranked him as the 67th richest American, putting his net worth at more than $1.7 million in October 1996.
The 18-page will filed Thursday in Manhattan Surrogate Court was dated Jan. 25, 1994.
Helmsley married his wife, the former Leona Mindy Rosenthal, a real estate executive, in 1972 after divorcing his wife of 33 years. It was a second marriage for both. The couple had no children.

In the late 1980s, the couple were indicted in a federal income tax evasion and mail fraud case. Helmsley was ruled unfit to stand trial because of ill health. Mrs. Helmsley, dubbed "the Queen of Mean" during the trial because of her fiery temper and harsh manner, was convicted and given a 32-month prison sentence, ordered to pay $7.1 million in fines and do 750 hours of community service. The sentence was later reduced to 21 months.

Helmsley was buried Tuesday at a private funeral service attended by 80 relatives and associates inside a granite mausoleum in Woodlawn Cemetery in New York. The monument has stained glass windows representing the New York City skyline.
